sectionSubtitle: Holistic care for body, mind and gut-brain axis

quotes.quote1: Your body is not failing; it is navigating an inflammatory process that needs patience and gentle time.
quotes.quote2: The fatigue and discomfort of UC are real. Honor your body's signals and allow yourself to rest without guilt.
quotes.quote3: The gut and brain communicate constantly. Calming your breath and mind is an active part of your healing.
quotes.quote4: A day with more bowel movements does not erase your progress. Breathe gently: one moment at a time.

guidelinesAccordion.title: Practical Care Guidelines
guidelinesAccordion.subtitle: Tap to view recommended care
guidelinesAccordion.hydrationDesc: During periods of loose stool or diarrhea, replenish fluids with water, oral rehydration salts, and coconut water to prevent electrolyte loss.
guidelinesAccordion.foodDesc: Opt for smaller portions throughout the day. Avoid ultra-processed, spicy, or high-caffeine foods that may irritate your mucosal lining.
guidelinesAccordion.restDesc: Stress activates inflammatory pathways in the bowel. Gentle breathing pauses and quality rest help soothe the gut-brain axis.

gastroCard.title: Medical Team & Gastroenterologist
gastroCard.desc: If symptoms persist for over 48 hours or fever occurs, contact your GI specialist. Never adjust medication doses alone.

psychoCard.title: Emotional Wellbeing & Mental Health
psychoCard.desc: Living with IBD affects emotions and sleep. Specialized therapy provides valuable support for stress and gut health.
